recipes.name: Frozen Chocolate Chip Cookie Dough Balls

steps.text: Beat together brown sugar and butter in a large bowl until creamy. Stir in flour, chocolate chips, walnuts, vanilla, and water; mix until dough is well blended.
Roll dough into bite-sized balls or use a small ice cream scoop. Place on a baking sheet and freeze until firm, about 2 hours. Store balls in resealable plastic bags in the freezer.

raw_recipe.headline: Frozen Chocolate Chip Cookie Dough Balls
raw_recipe.description: Little chocolate chip cookie dough balls combine classic ingredients into appealing frozen treats for all ages. Junior cooks will have fun making them, too.

review.reviewBody: Superb frozen treat. For those who found it to be too bland, add 1/8 tsp salt, which will bring the flavor to life. Also added a pinch of soda, since all chocolate chip cookie dough recipes have soda, and it tasted like the real thing. It was very soft, but I had no problem rolling into balls. I used them to bake into the cupcake recipe on this site (long name, like Choc. Chip Cookie Dough + Cupcake...) because the dough mixture in that recipe features eggs, and since it is not supposed to bake all the way through, I used this one instead as it does not feature the use of raw eggs. Absolutely perfect.

We love this recipe but I have a WARNING. I found out today that you should use heat-treated flour (never heard of it before) because regular flour might have bacterial contamination. I thought leaving out the egg made it safe but apparently not. We only made this once and LOVED it. Great for making something on a hot day and was easy for all the kids to make. Very sad about the flour issue but some sites say you can heat treat your own flour so that might be a good idea.
I made a few changes. I used 1 cup brown sugar and half cup raspberry jam. Refrigerated till solid, then dipped them in dark chocolate

I would definitely make these again. I followed other recommendations to add 1/8 teaspoon salt, 1/4 teaspoon of baking soda and did 1 cup brown sugar and 1/2 cup white sugar. I also used 60% cacao dark choc chips with a little instant coffee added to it once melted to dip them in.

Wendy's fast food restaurants have what is called a Chocolate Chip Cookie Dough blizzard or freeze. It's vanilla ice cream with a mix-in of these round, small bits of heaven in the form of chocolate chip cookie dough yumminess! THIS is what this recipe provides. As a surprise for our recently Jr. High graduate son's party I made this recipe. The ONLY changes I made for us is NO WALNUTS (to ME AKA I call them 'dirt clods' lol) and I added the whole two cup bag of chocolate chips. This provided the mix to go further for the party and also a guaranteed chip in every cluster! Rather than the messiness of forming the 'balls' of dough by hand, I used two small measuring spoons and scooped up the dough with one and dropped little piles of the soft dough onto two cookie sheets. I froze them in the freezer for only 30 mins and then spatula'ed them into a ziploc bag and back into the freezer until dessert time. I got rave, rave reviews with this recipe. You will too. On the make-your-own-sundae bar our guests sprinkled the dough bits on top of scooped vanilla ice cream and drizzled hot fudge and topped everything with Cool Whip in a can spray. You won't regret this one people. :)
Great recipe! We melted chocolate in a double boiler and dipped the frozen balls into the chocolate and then refroze. My daughters want to add sprinkles next time.

We LOVED these! If you love cookie dough, you will love these! I did make a few changes though, which is why I am only giving this 4 stars. As is, it deserves 4 stars. I used 1 cup brown sugar and 1/2 cup white sugar, 1/8 teaspoon salt, and a whole bag of normal sized chocolate chips. I like it better when there is chocolate in every bite. I made them a very decent size, yet they made more than expected, which was a plus! Also, I put them into the freezer for about an hour and then dipped some of them in chocolate. They were great and looked amazing! If you dip them in chocolate or not, they still look and taste fine. Also, I found that in the freezer it froze a little too much, so instead I put them in a container and placed them in the coldest part of the fridge. They are still great, and I reccomend eating them directly from the fridge/freezer.

I made this recipe a few days ago & it was delicious to all family! I used white chocolate chips which i melted & mixed in with the batter. I used an electric mixer to mix ingredients & it worked well. One thing though, I thought the batter would have been too messy to make balls with so I placed the batter by one spoon full in cupcake liners and froze. So I'm curious how others made these into balls. I'm wondering if this batter could be baked. That's for another day,lol

These are simple and taste great. I ended up covering the dough balls with tempered white chocolate, and it worked well to keep the ball firm while eating it. If you eat just the cookie dough it softens quickly it your hands, so eat quickly. :) A tip for rolling them into balls- scoop out teaspoon sized lumps onto the cookie sheets and freeze for 30 minutes. Take them out and they should be firm enough to roll in your hands.

So yummy! These were a total hit. They are better on day two, and even more yummy if they thaw a little bit :) I used 1 cup brown sugar and 1/2 cup white sugar...I also added a little salt because I love it with my chocolate! Dipped in Almond Bark and decorated with festive sprinkles.

Nauseatingly sweet. I added about 1/2 tsp. of salt because I like my chocolate chip cookies with salt. I also used 1/2 cup white sugar and 1 cup brown sugar. That made them perfect. I melted a 12-oz. bag of semi-sweet chocolate chips with 2 Tbsp. Crisco, and dipped and drizzled all the balls. They were really good. The kids went nuts over RAW COOKIE DOUGH!!!!!
Instead of adding 3/4 cup chocolate chips and 3/4 cup walnuts, I added 1 1/2 cups of chocolate chips and turned out to be, um, interesting flavor and good enough. thanks. I'll try adding salt!
Mixed ingredients like it said and was very dry and bland. I’m upset I wasted the ingredients I had when I already had a recipe for cookie dough that works amazing and taste great.
So tastie

Kids loved these, I added the 1/8 teaspoon salt as another reviewer suggested. I also melted and drizzled chocolate on top. You could add sprinkles inside with the choco chips that would be tasty too.
Amazing

I love cookie dough, so these were great! I made some with the chocolate coating and some without for a Christmas party, and found that the ones without the coating were more popular! They are a bit hard to bite into when they come out of the cold, but I let them warm up for a good fifteen minutes and they were perfect. Will be making these again!
It tastes amazing! Super fun to make too!!!!
I would suggest melting chocolate and covering the balls with it I use Toll House semi-sweet chocolate chips but any kind would work fine, my family loves them!
